questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language was a crucial aspect for me, understanding the patients in their language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough, some of he information was hard to find than other.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a meeting with the host exchange coordinator, because I missed the introduction day there I could get answers to my questions, information about MRSA screening access and student cards.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Studio apartments, single apartments with kitchens, shared flats with 2 to 4 People. Two housing locations. Ranging in price.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchens were fully equipped, no meal plan services.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can pick the accommodation type according to your price range and thought I would recommend shared kitchens for the social aspect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Once you had the required documents, it was easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you had to fill out an online application form, and send in your transcript of records and recommendation from your University along with a copy of your passport. After that you fill out the information in the host universities mobility-online where you then can select and prioritise courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact the Contact person/Exchange coordinator at the respective universities for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registering of courses was a prioritising system. I got my first two priorities of departments and after a dialogue with the exchange coordinator at the host university found a third course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open minded, start collecting the documents early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My exchange was exclusively clinical rotations. The level was matched to my knowledge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was similar to my university. The teaching was primarily case based and procedure training.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical rotation in the emergency process - 2EE090
Clinical rotation in surgery 1 - 2EE036
Clinical rotation in surgery 2 - 2EE037

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend all of these courses. Since these were clinical rotations individual preference  in specialties going to impact your view of it. The emergency rotation was interesting because of the Södersjukhuset had primarily acute specialists on staff instead of a representative of a specialties working in the emergency room, which gives a broad perspective that was interesting to see.
The surgery courses was where really good for someone interested in surgery, with opportunities to participate in ward tasks and assistant surgery.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There’s an open gym, outdoor tennis court, beach volleyball. Student club with events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend visiting the tourist places, the museums. It is a new city to explore

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I can recommend taking the ferry to health game or the train to Corona sailing in the archipelago. Some museums have free entry for students on certain days.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is similar to my culture so it was not hard to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Primarily got to know international exchange students, because I only had rotation with exchange students. so I have no tips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate the fika culture, And bringing leftovers for lunch.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would tell them to start looking into exchange early, The whole process takes a while.
I would recommend choosing housing with other people, and attending the introduction day and social events where everybody is looking for a friend, it can be challenging later on. I would recommend learning Swedish it makes the whole exchange better.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I recommend arriving a few business days before your first
day.there
are a lot of practical things that need to be taken care of like getting access cards and student cards.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the scene has been seeing that I am capable to adapt to new situations and settings, to work in a team of doctors and nurses. To have made new friends from all over the world, And connections for the future. It has given me the opportunity to see and live in a different culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The most challenging thing during this exchange has been managing my expectation of myself, to be OK with leaving the tourist activities to the weekend, because clinical rotations take a lot of energy especially in a new language. Not having been able to see everything I wanted here, just mean I have an excuse to come back.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
